subject: VPC inference allocator: capacity projection and allocation play
messages:
From: Carlos Ramirez <c.ramirez@novatek.ai>

Cc: procurement@novatek.ai
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Planning call follow-up — allocator sizing for private VPC deployment

Thanks for the call this morning, Stephanie. Quick summary and a couple asks from our infra team: we want to target 1200 concurrent inference sessions across two regions (primary + DR), 95th p95 token latency target ~180ms, and support mixed workloads (short chat-like queries and occasional long-batch embeddings).

Questions:
- Can Redwood provide a projection for GPU count and headroom assumptions given mixed QPS (50% short requests, 40% medium, 10% long)?
- Any recommended allocation strategy for the allocator layer so we can keep burst costs predictable in our VPC?

Please send any supporting modeling or a one-page play that we can push to our procurement team.

--
Carlos Ramirez
Head of Platform
Novatek Robotics
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Carlos Ramirez <c.ramirez@novatek.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2027 13:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Planning call follow-up — allocator sizing for private VPC deployment

Carlos — thanks, great to align. Attaching a short model (allocator_modeling.xlsx) and a VPC topology sketch (vpc_topology_v2.drawio) with conservative assumptions and an ops play. High-level answers below; full assumptions are in the spreadsheet.

TL;DR summary:
- Baseline GPUs (sustained): 18 A100 equivalent GPUs per region to meet 95th p95 latency at expected sustained QPS with ~25% headroom.
- Burst buffer / warm pool: additional 6 GPUs per region as pre-warmed capacity for <5s cold-starts and to absorb short spikes.
- Allocation policy: ratio-based allocator that reserves 60% capacity for short low-latency requests and 40% for medium/long workloads with a small preemptible burst band for background/embeddings jobs.

Operational notes:
- We recommend rolling canary policies for initial traffic ramp (20% -> 50% -> 100% over 3 days).
- Network egress: allow 1.2Gbps per GPU pod peak; the topology file shows recommended private peering and subnet segmentation.

I'll highlight the key rows in the spreadsheet and propose we sync on Thurs to run through the numbers with your infra team.

Attachments: [attachment: allocator_modeling.xlsx (spreadsheet, 140KB)], [attachment: vpc_topology_v2.drawio (diagram, 520KB)]

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Planning call follow-up — allocator sizing for private VPC deployment

All — I pulled a quick sensitivity table into the spreadsheet (tab: sensitivity). Two follow-ups from my side before Thurs:
1) Can Novatek confirm the percent of requests that include >8k tokens? The long-tail heavily affects warm-pool sizing.
2) Network topology: are you planning to route all egress through the same NAT gateway or per-subnet NATs? Egress contention changes our recommended pre-warm size.

Quick note on the allocator behavior we propose: when utilization >70% for >30s, allocator starts migrating/circuit-breaking lower-priority background jobs and signals to autoscaler to pre-provision burst GPUs. We recommend a two-stage pre-warm (warm-cache at per-GPU process level + instance warm pool) to keep token latency within p95 targets for short queries.

Ben
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Thanks — answers inline:
- We estimate ~8% of requests will be >8k tokens (larger embeddings and diagnostics pipelines).
- We'll use a single NAT per-region with capacity headroom managed by infra; we can add per-subnet NATs later if needed.

Next steps:
- Please finalize the spreadsheet numbers with the 8% long request assumption and include a short note for procurement that summarizes committed baseline GPUs, optional burst pay-as-you-go units, and expected monthly egress.
- Can Redwood provide a short amendment template (one page) that lists dedicated pool sizes, SLAs for throughput/latency, and billing rules for burst usage? Procurement wants something to review before our Thurs call.

I'll be available for the Thurs sync at 11:00 PT.
